question: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the official languages recognized by the Indian government.
 
• As of now, there are 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
 
• These languages include Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, and others.
 
• The Constitution originally included 14 languages in the Eighth Schedule, but subsequent amendments have increased the number to 22.
 
• Languages in the Eighth Schedule are given official status and are promoted for development by the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **22 Official Languages:**

 
 
• The 22 languages are Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• Article 343 to 351 of the Indian Constitution deal with the official language of the Republic of India.
 
 
 
• **Language Commission:**
 
 
• The Constitution provides for the appointment of a Commission to make recommendations for the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes and for the restriction on the use of English for all or any of the official purposes of the Union.
 
 
 
• **Official Language Act:**
 
 
• The Official Languages Act, 1963, and its subsequent amendments outline the provisions for the languages to be used for official purposes of the Union and for transaction of business in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Languages:**
 
 
• The government has established various institutions and schemes for the promotion and development of languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
